question: Which part of the food is defecated?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Unused food**__ .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Vitamins can be categorized based on their solubility: water-soluble and fat-soluble.

__
 
• Vitamin A is fat-soluble.
 
• Vitamin B is water-soluble.
 
• Vitamin C is water-soluble.
 
• Vitamin K is fat-soluble.
 
• Vitamin D is fat-soluble.

Water-soluble vitamins, such as Vitamin C, dissolve in water and are typically not stored in large amounts in the body. They need to be consumed more regularly in the diet. On the other hand, fat-soluble vitamins (such as A, D, and K) are absorbed along with fats in the diet and can be stored in the body's fatty tissues.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Glucose:**

 
 
• Glucose is a simple sugar and an essential carbohydrate in biology, serving as a primary energy source for cells.
 
• It is crucial for cellular respiration, where cells convert glucose and oxygen into energy, carbon dioxide, and water.
 
 
• The body regulates glucose levels in the blood through hormones like insulin and glucagon, produced by the pancreas.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Nutrients:**
 
 
• Nutrients are substances obtained from food that are vital for growth, energy, and maintaining bodily functions.
 
• They are classified into macronutrients (carbohydrates, proteins, fats) and micronutrients (vitamins, minerals), each playing unique roles in the body.
 
• Proper intake of a balanced mix of these nutrients is essential for overall health and prevention of diseases.
